runner.text:
# Brief for the coach

## What I was looking at

Two training setups exist side by side, and everything I ran so far was read-only — nothing has been changed, proposed, or sent to the athlete's logging app.

**The older setup** holds the previous programme: a ten-session rotation across Week A and Week B, built around the Tuesday evening personal-trainer session, plus two optional conditioning sessions (a quiet strength circuit and a kettlebell-swing clock session). The profile there says the athlete trains six days, rests Thursday, and that the Tuesday PT session alternates chest/back with legs/core and is programmed by the trainer, not by the athlete.

**The newer setup** is the live engine. It is on its third programme version, an amendment adopted on 4 November 2026 with a hypertrophy emphasis. The stated reason for the amendment was that the engine could now count pull-up variants toward a real dose target, and that a conditioning session could sit next to a lifting day — so the swing finisher was moved out of the Monday session into its own clock session. The programme view returned **no warnings**.

## The current programme (third version, adopted 4 November 2026)

Ten sessions. The two PT sessions carry no prescribed lines because the trainer controls them; the engine just estimates what they contribute.

**PT · chest and back** (gym, weekly, core) — estimated 6 hard sets chest, 6 lats, 3 biceps.
**PT · legs and core** (gym, weekly, core) — estimated 6 quadriceps, 4 glutes, 4 abdominals.

**Monday · overhead press, back and arms** — 75 minutes, core.
- Overhead Press (Barbell): warm-up 1×5, warm-up 1×3, then a top set of 5 at RPE 8 and 4 back-off sets of 6 (top-set-and-back-off scheme).
- Chest Supported Row (Dumbbell): 4×8–12 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Lateral Raise (Dumbbell): 3×12–15 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Rear Delt Fly (Dumbbell): 3×12–15 at RPE 8, double progression.

**Wednesday · pull-up volume and core** — 75 minutes, core.
- Scapular Pull Up: 2 activation sets of 6–8 at RPE 5.
- Negative Pull Up: 3×2–4 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Pull Up (Band): 4×5–8 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Flexed Arm Hang: 2 holds of 20 seconds.
- Lying Leg Raise: 3×10–15 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Suitcase Carry: 4 carries of 30 seconds.
- Single Leg Standing Calf Raise (Dumbbell): 3×10–15 at RPE 8, double progression.

**Friday · strict pull-up test, squat and legs** — 75 minutes, core.
- Pull Up: 1 single at RPE 10 (the strict test).
- Back Squat (Barbell): warm-ups of 5, 3 and 2, then a top set of 5 at RPE 8 and 4 back-off sets of 5.
- Romanian Deadlift (Barbell): 3×6–10 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Split Squat (Dumbbell): 3×8–12 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Shoulder Press (Dumbbell): 3×8–12 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Single Leg Standing Calf Raise (Dumbbell): 3×10–15 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Ab Wheel Rollout: 3×6–12 at RPE 8, double progression.

**Saturday · bench, back and arms** — 90 minutes, core.
- Bench Press (Barbell): warm-ups of 8, 5 and 3, then a top set of 5 at RPE 8 and 4 back-off sets of 6.
- Bent Over Row (Barbell): 4×6–10 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Incline Bench Press (Dumbbell): 3×8–12 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Dip Negatives: 3×3–5 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Overhead Triceps Extension (Dumbbell): 3×10–15 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Lateral Raise (Dumbbell): 3×12–15 at RPE 8, double progression.

**Sunday · deadlift and legs** — 90 minutes, core.
- Deadlift (Barbell): warm-ups of 5 and 3, then a top set of 5 at RPE 8 and 3 back-off sets of 5.
- Bulgarian Split Squat (Dumbbell): 3×8–12 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Hip Thrust (Barbell): 3×8–12 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Pull Up (Band): 3×5–8 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Bicep Curl (Dumbbell): 3×8–12 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Hammer Curl (Dumbbell): 3×10–12 at RPE 8, double progression.
- Farmers Walk (Dumbbell): 3 carries of 30 seconds.

**Conditioning · kettlebell swing on the clock** — optional, weekly. Every minute on the minute for 12 minutes, 12 swings per minute at RPE 7. Progresses in 2-minute steps up to a cap of 16 minutes, and reps can rise to a cap of 15 per minute.

**Conditioning · strength circuit** — optional, standing. 4 rounds (cap 6) inside a 16-minute time cap at RPE 8: Goblet Squat 10, Ring Push Up 12, Kettlebell Swing 12, Mountain Climber 16 per round.

**Daily · dead hang** — optional, daily. 2 hangs of 20 seconds at RPE 5.

Current working loads are not in the programme view; they live in the week plan, which I haven't pulled yet.

## What the older programme looked like (for comparison)

The one old session I saw in full was the Week A Friday push day, with its starting loads in pounds:
- Overhead Press (Barbell): warm-ups 1×5 and 1×3, then 4×5–6 at RPE 8, started at 75 lb, 180 s rest, add 5 lb once every set hits the top of the range.
- Incline Bench Press (Dumbbell): 3×8–10 at RPE 8, started at 30 lb per hand, 120 s rest, add 5 lb per hand.
- Lateral Raise (Dumbbell): 4×12–15 at RPE 8, started at 7.5 lb per hand, 60 s rest, add 2.5 lb per hand.
- Overhead Triceps Extension (Dumbbell): 3×10–12 at RPE 9, started at 30 lb, 90 s rest, add 5 lb.
- Assisted Dip (Machine): 3×6–10 at RPE 8.5, started at 30 lb of assistance, 90 s rest, progressing down a ladder of 30 → 20 → 10 → 0 lb assist at 10 reps for 3 sets.
- Chest Fly (Dumbbell): 3×12–15 at RPE 8, started at 15 lb per hand, 75 s rest, add 2.5 lb per hand.

The old rotation covered a broader exercise menu (assisted pull-ups, inverted rows, straight-arm band pulldowns, incline curls, hollow and arch holds, hanging leg raises, side planks, lunges, seated calf raises) that the new programme has slimmed down.

## Warnings

None were returned. Nothing is currently flagged against training.

## Proposed changes

None yet. There are draft documents in the new setup dated 1, 2 and 4 November 2026 (check-in, exercises, goal, plan, profile, and three programme drafts), but the only one acted on is the programme amendment adopted on 4 November. No week plan has been proposed or pushed in this session, so there is nothing the athlete needs to agree to right now. One check-in is on record, dated 1 November 2026.

first.text:
Here's what's dropped out between your old routine and the plan you're on now. I went through the old rotation and matched it against every session in the current one; anything that moved to a close variant I've noted rather than counted as missing.

**Gone from the plan entirely**

Pull / back
- Assisted pull-ups (machine) — the band pull-ups, negatives and the Friday strict test cover the same job now, so this is a swap rather than a loss.
- Inverted rows — nothing horizontal-bodyweight in the new plan; rows are now chest-supported dumbbell on Monday and barbell bent-over on Saturday.
- Straight-arm band pulldowns — no lat isolation at all now; lats come only from the pull-up work and the two rows.

Push
- Chest fly (dumbbell) — no chest isolation now; chest is bench, incline dumbbell press and the dip negatives.
- Assisted dips (machine) — replaced by dip negatives on Saturday.

Arms
- Incline curls — curls are now standing dumbbell and hammer curls on Sunday.

Core
- Hollow holds and arch holds
- Hanging leg raises — replaced by lying leg raises on Wednesday.
- Side planks — the suitcase carry on Wednesday is the only anti-lateral work left.

Legs
- Lunges — split squats and Bulgarian split squats took this slot.
- Seated calf raises — calves are now single-leg standing raises twice a week; nothing seated, so the soleus gets less direct work.

**Still in, same or near-identical**
Overhead press, incline dumbbell bench, lateral raises, overhead triceps extension, kettlebell swings, the strength circuit, dead hangs, squat, deadlift, RDL, hip thrust, farmers walk.

The ones I'd actually look twice at, if you miss them: side planks or a hollow hold (cheap to add, the core work now is all flexion plus one carry), straight-arm pulldowns if your lats feel undertrained relative to your arms on pull-ups, and seated calf raises if your calves have been a priority. The rest were mostly replaced by something that does the same thing.

Tell me which, if any, you want back and I'll show you exactly where they'd slot in and what would have to give way for time. Nothing changes until you say so.
